title: Which open hydraulic circuit gets a small excavator closest to stock energy use for the least money?
lede: research programme (proposal stage): pump-shaft energy of fixed open-centre, load-sensing and ideal independent-metering circuits on an illustrative excavator cycle; over 2,916 swept cases load-sensing uses a median 47% of open-centre energy and metering 80% of load-sensing, an ordering that holds by construction; on 20,000 random cycles in a machine envelope load-sensing is a median 44% of open-centre; no measured cycle, margin or price is sourced yet
summary: An open research programme on which hydraulic circuit a small shop can build from catalogue parts to get a 1.5 to 3 t excavator closest to stock energy use, and at what parts cost. Milestone 1 is a stdlib model of pump-shaft energy for three circuits (fixed-displacement open-centre, load-sensing, ideal independent metering; analytic single-actuator check, 6 tests) and a 2,916-case grid on one four-phase cycle: load-sensing uses a median 47% of open-centre shaft energy (22 to 81%), saving more as flow demand falls (31%, 47%, 63% of open-centre at 0.5, 0.75 and 1.0 of full flow), and metering uses a median 80% of load-sensing, 88% with equal actuator pressures and 74% at 1.5 times the reference spread. The ordering holds in every case but only because each rung removes a loss term, so it is a code check rather than a finding. The cycle, pressures, flows and margins are illustrative values written from memory and swept, not sourced; there are no dynamics, leakage, line losses, energy recovery or parts costs; the DOI registry was unreachable so references were checked by web search, not cite_check. Milestone 2a repeats the comparison on 20,000 random cycles inside a machine envelope (pump 45 L/min, 20 to 180 bar, taken from an unopened search summary of one mini-excavator listing): load-sensing uses a median 44% of open-centre energy, metering 72% of load-sensing (87% at equal actuator pressures), and H3 fails per case in about a third of equal-pressure cycles. The cycles are random, not measured. Preliminary; arithmetic only, nothing run on a machine.
